referenceSize.note: SeaLifeBase lists a maximum of 40 cm WD; the UQ Great Barrier Reef Invertebrates fact sheet (Laxton 1974, Heron Island) gives adults over 20 cm across with a 30-40 mm disc and 80-120 mm arms, so 25 cm tip to tip is a typical large adult. Measured across the widest pair of arm tips (xy extent).

palette._note: Display-referred sRGB-encoded values: lib.textures.write_image stores albedo bytes verbatim and tags the image sRGB.

morphology.notes: Five long, nearly uniform cylindrical arms with rounded tips meeting at a very small central disc (Laxton 1974: disc diameter 30-40 mm, arm length 80-120 mm on Heron Island adults). Arm reach about six disc radii; arm thickness about 2.2 cm; aboral side convex, oral side flattened with a shallow ambulacral groove; arm tips held a few millimetres off the substrate.

visualDebt: Arms are straight tubes; live animals often show slight lateral arm curvature and per-individual length asymmetry beyond the mild front/side/rear variation modelled here.
Granules are a normal-map relief only; no modelled plate geometry.
Ambulacral groove is a shallow cross-section dip with painted tube feet; no individual tube-foot geometry.
Disc and arm bases are overlapping closed solids; the interradial crotch is an intersection crease rather than a blended surface.
Hub dome is about 4.6 cm across interradially, slightly larger than the 3-4 cm disc Laxton (1974) measured, because it must cover the five arm-tube junctions.
